newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico's tribes sign new gaming agreements.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico's tribes sign new gaming agreements.

text.p: Ten of New Mexico's Indian tribes entered into new gaming agreements with the state Tuesday, opening the way for the legalization of casino gambling on their lands.
Gov. Gary Johnson signed the gaming agreements, or "compacts," to replace previous ones declared illegal by state and federal courts last year.

Tribal leaders said they were unhappy with terms requiring them to pay more of their gaming revenues to the state government, but they agreed to the new compacts because they feared their casinos might otherwise be shut down.
"It's almost extortion," said Wendell Chino, president of the Mescalero Apache tribe in southern New Mexico. "We have signed under protest."
Before the compacts can become law, they must be approved by Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt.

Chino said he hoped Babbitt would declare the revenue sections of the compacts to be in violation of federal law and send them back to New Mexico for negotiations between tribes and the state legislature.

Johnson and the tribes drew up the previous compacts in 1995 but they failed to seek the state legislature's approval, and the agreements were declared illegal by state and federal courts. The legislature has approved the new compacts signed by Johnson Tuesday.
The tribes had been allowed to keep their casinos open pending resolution of the legal dispute.

Frank Chaves, co-chair of the New Mexico Indian Gaming Association, said the tribes had expected the Supreme Court to rule against it on the old compacts and thus agreed to cut a new deal with the state legislature.
"We currently have no other option but to go with the compacts," Chaves said.
